- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#11 ("Version 1 review: confirm the text; baselines not run (cluster HT, GNN)") by `experiment-repo`  > **GNN baseline: delivered on `dev` (`results/gnn_cells.csv` + `.meta.json`; code `scripts/run_gnn.py`, `src/gate/gnn.py` in the code archive, `analysis/make_gnn.py` aggregates).** Cluster HT was confirmed earlier (#4).
  > 
  > **What it is.** A two-layer mean-aggregation GNN (hidden 16) on the observed graph; node input = own treatment, mean neighbour treatment, standardised log degree. Adam, weight decay and epochs chosen by a graph-cluster hold-out (Louvain folds, nodes next to the held-out fold removed) plus the corner loss used for the other Tier A learners. Estimate = mean prediction at (z=1, f=1) minus at (z=0, f=0): the same corner as every other estimator. Same assignments, graphs, noise and folds as the Tier A runs (`chin_check_max_abs_diff` = 0: the Chin estimate recomputed inside the run equals the Tier A array).
  > 
  > **What it was computed on.** Tier A, Bernoulli design, noise multiple 0.5, s = 0.5, mechanisms a–f plus the null column. **13 of the 14 Tier A cells**: the SBM n=3000, d=80, p=0.25 cell did not finish (its job was ended at the 4 h limit with no output); it is absent, not zero. Only the first 10 of the 40 assignments of each of the 5 graph draws are used (50 draws; real graphs: 1 graph, first 50 of 200 assignments), and every other estimator is scored on the same draws. This is a reduced run: the GNN costs 3.5–4.1 h per cell on this host. Rows: 13 cells × 7 columns × 8 estimators (A_ada has 84 rather than 91 rows where it is undefined).
  > 
  > **Result (91 cell-mechanism rows, 6 mechanisms + null, RMSE of the normalised error).** Median RMSE: Chin 0.218, GNN 0.333, A_hgb 0.401, A_ada 0.405, A_rf 0.422, A_lasso 0.457, dm 0.499, A_ridge 0.624. Mean rank over the 91 rows (1 = best): Chin 1.80, GNN 3.40, A_hgb 4.40, A_ada 4.76, dm 4.82, A_lasso 5.13, A_rf 5.32, A_ridge 6.12. Best estimator in a row: Chin 59, dm 18, A_ada 4, A_ridge 3, GNN 2, A_hgb 2, A_lasso 2, A_rf 1. Paired log RMSE ratio of the GNN: to dm, 57 of 91 intervals below 0 and 27 above (median −0.25); to Chin, 5 below and 66 above (median +0.37). So the GNN is the best of the learners but is worse than Chin's regression in most cells; mechanism (d) (threshold) is the one where it is not worse (mean log ratio to Chin −0.10 over 13 cells; the only 5 intervals below 0 against Chin are (d) cells: BA, ER, SBM d=20, SBM d=80 p=0.5, WS). The null column (13 rows) is where it is clearly worse than dm (mean log ratio +1.69); on the six mechanisms alone the mean log ratio to dm is −0.34.
  > 
  > **What this does and does not support.** The text may say a GNN was run on 13 of the 14 Tier A cells on a 50-draw subset, with these fixed settings (one architecture, hidden width 16, no tuning of the architecture), and that it does not beat the exposure-mapping regression. It must not say the GNN was tuned to its best or that a larger or differently built GNN would not win. Not run: the SBM d=80, p=0.25 cell, and any GNN on Tier G or the cluster designs.
  > 
  > Please also check the table numbers above against `gnn_cells.csv` when you write them (the estimator column is `A_gnn`, `log_ratio_vs_dm`, `log_ratio_vs_chin` with `_lo`/`_hi`).
